GeometricSatakeAndFusion.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has perfectoid spaces, diamonds, v-sheaves, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, loop groups, affine or Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannians, Schubert cells, perverse sheaves, universal local acyclicity, hyperbolic localization or any six-operation formalism; 'Satake', 'Schubert', 'Perverse' and 'Fargues' each have zero hits in the declaration index and in both Lean trees. What the libraries do supply are inputs, not targets: Mathlib's Witt vectors, perfection and tilting/untilting, its module Grassmannian, its abstract t-structures, derived categories and symmetric monoidal categories; Tau Ceti's simply connected root data for every Dynkin type, its Chevalley involution on the Geck carrier, and its Tannakian reconstruction for a commutative Hopf algebra. Two things the roadmap treats as work are closer to done than it suggests: the pinned dual root datum as combinatorial data (TauCeti.DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum together with RootPairing.flip), and the abstract double-coset Hecke ring that the classical Satake comparison needs (Mathlib.NumberTheory.HeckeRing). Genuinely missing is everything geometric: the loop-group and Schubert geometry of GS0, the Bhatt-Scholze projectivity route (no ample, nef or semiample line bundles exist in either library), the relative perverse t-structure of GS1, convolution and fusion, and the Tannakian identification with the pinned dual group.

targets.target: Positive and full loop groups L+G, LG over Div^d_Y from a split reductive O_E-model
targets.note: Neither library has loop groups of a group scheme: grep -c for LoopGroup in declarations.tsv is 0 and no Lean file in either tree mentions L+G/LG. The Fargues-Fontaine curve, Div^d_Y and B_D^+ are absent too.

targets.target: The etale quotient LG/L+G and the double-quotient local Hecke stack
targets.note: Mathlib has stacks only as CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack (a descent condition on a pseudofunctor); there is no algebraic or v-stack theory and no quotient-stack construction anywhere in either tree.

targets.target: Descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti has faithfully flat descent for algebra maps in the affine setting only; there is no descent of finite projective modules along the completed rings of a divisor on the FF curve, and no B_dR^+ at all.

targets.target: Relative Grassmannian of a G-bundle trivialized off ordered leg divisors; Beauville-Laszlo gluing
targets.note: Mathlib's Module.Grassmannian is the functor of submodules with locally free quotient of fixed rank (EGA I.9.7.3), representability still a TODO. It is not the affine/BD Grassmannian. grep -c -i Beauville in declarations.tsv is 0 and neither tree mentions Beauville-Laszlo.

targets.target: v-sheaf representability and local spatiality in legs
targets.note: No diamonds, v-sheaves or v-topology exist in either library; grep -rn -i for 'v-sheaf' and 'diamond' in the Lean sources returns only unrelated uses of the word diamond (diamond inheritance, Data/UInt).

targets.target: Bounded relative position by dominant cocharacters; Schubert cells and closures, properness, dimension <2rho,mu>, closure relations
targets.note: grep -c -i Schubert in declarations.tsv is 0 and grep -rn -i Schubert in both Lean trees returns nothing; no affine flag variety and no Demazure resolution (the only 'Demazure' hits are bibliographic references to SGA III and prose about the Chevalley--Demazure construction).

duplicates.note: GS.1 also constructs the Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian, bounded Hecke stacks and collision/factorization maps, over powers of a curve in equal characteristic; its own text says it is a separate classical proof even where this mixed-characteristic API is reusable.
ET.2b constructs equal-characteristic affine Grassmannians and affine Springer fibres with their Picard actions and finite-type quotients for the Hitchin fibration.

targets.target: Truncated positive loop groups and their congruence filtration by vector-group quotients
targets.note: No loop groups exist in either library, so no truncation or congruence filtration of one does either.

targets.target: ell-cohomological smoothness of the open cell Gr_(G,mu) of ell-dimension <2rho,mu> (FS VI.2.4/IV.1.18)
targets.note: Cohomological smoothness is a notion for morphisms of v-stacks; neither library has the six-operation formalism on diamonds in which it is stated.

targets.target: Identification of a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and positive-loop unipotent fibres
targets.note: No Schubert cells in either tree; Tau Ceti's flag-variety material stops at abstract root-system and Coxeter combinatorics.

targets.target: VI.2.8's explicit congruence bound from the weights of mu on Lie G
targets.note: No such bound; Tau Ceti's weight theory (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Weights) is about Lie-algebra weight spaces, not congruence levels of a loop group.

targets.target: Descent of the Galois-orbit cells over a splitting field
targets.note: Galois descent exists in Tau Ceti only for group algebras, lattices and representations, not for Schubert cells of a Grassmannian that does not exist.

duplicates.note: BG2:smooth-Artin is the named consumer of exactly this smoothness statement; it imports rather than restates it.

targets.target: Witt-vector lattice functor on perfect residue algebras and its bounded subfunctors
targets.note: Mathlib has the ramified-free Witt vectors W(R), truncated Witt vectors, Frobenius, Verschiebung, Teichmuller and the perfection/tilting functors, but no lattice functor L -> W(R)-lattices in W(R)[1/p]^n and no bounded subfunctors; grep -i 'WittVector.*lattice' in declarations.tsv is empty. The roadmap's ramified Witt algebra (RF0) is also absent.

targets.target: Perfectly finitely presented Grassmannian/flag spaces, Demazure resolutions, relative-position strata
targets.note: Neither library has perfect schemes as a geometric category (Mathlib's PerfectRing/IsPerfectClosure is ring-theoretic), nor the Witt Grassmannian, nor a Demazure resolution.

targets.target: h/v-descent for vector bundles on perfect schemes (BS17 SS2-4)
targets.note: Mathlib's descent theory for schemes is for the Zariski, etale and (new) pro-etale precoverages on Scheme; there is no h- or v-topology and no descent theorem for vector bundles along it.

targets.target: Bhatt-Scholze projectivity: geometric determinant line on a Demazure resolution and the trivial-on-geometric-fibres descent criterion (BS17 6.8/6.12)
targets.note: Absent, and so is every ingredient: there is no determinant-of-cohomology line bundle and no Demazure resolution in either tree.

targets.target: Positivity/ampleness by the semiampleness criterion (BS17 SS7-8) and Keel's positive-characteristic criterion (exceptional locus of a nef bundle, Frobenius-power extension of sections, reduction to semiampleness)
targets.note: There is no ample, nef, semiample or big line bundle anywhere: grep -rn -i 'isAmple|ample line bundle|very ample' over both Lean trees returns nothing and 'semiample' has zero hits in declarations.tsv. Tau Ceti's AlgebraicGeometry/LineBundle has no positivity notions.

targets.target: The v-sheaf of these perfections identified with the special fibre of the GS0:loop-geometry Grassmannian; integral family and bounded properness
targets.note: Depends on objects neither library has.

duplicates.note: Same Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian and bounded Hecke stacks, in the equal-characteristic function-field setting.

targets.target: Positive-loop equivariance, orbit stratifications, semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata, with dimension estimates
targets.note: No loop groups, no semi-infinite orbits, no Schubert strata in either library.

targets.target: Finiteness for compact-support cohomology and hyperbolic-localization comparisons
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'hyperbolic localization' over both Lean trees returns nothing; there is no attractor/repeller formalism.

targets.target: Relative perverse t-structure on bounded constructible complexes with stalk/costalk inequalities and gluing across finite stratifications
targets.note: Mathlib has the abstract theory of t-structures on a triangulated category (TStructure, IsLE/IsGE, truncations) and derived categories of abelian categories, but no perverse t-structure on any geometric category: grep -c -i Perverse in declarations.tsv is 0 and neither Lean tree mentions perverse sheaves or recollement.

targets.target: Flat perverse objects versus arbitrary perverse objects in integral coefficients
targets.note: Depends on a perverse t-structure that does not exist.

targets.target: One-leg special/generic-fibre comparison on ULA, flat-perverse categories over Spd(O_C), Spd(C) and Spd(k-bar), full faithfulness and essential surjectivity (FS VI.5-VI.7)
targets.note: Universal local acyclicity is absent from both trees (grep -rn -i 'universally locally acyclic' returns nothing), as are Spd and adic spectra of perfectoid rings.

ET.2a re-exports the same EDC.0-5 scheme perverse foundation, so the scheme half of GS1's t-structure input has two other declared owners.

targets.target: Satake objects defined by equivariance, relative perversity, ULA and coefficient flatness (FS VI.6-VI.8)
targets.note: grep -c -i Satake in declarations.tsv is 0 and neither Lean tree mentions Satake; the defining conditions (relative perversity, ULA) are themselves absent.

targets.target: Convolution diagrams, the convolution map and the convolution operation by proper-support pushforward
targets.note: There is no proper pushforward of sheaves on v-stacks in either library; Mathlib's sheaf pushforward is the ordinary direct image on a site, with no exceptional functors.

targets.target: Ambient associativity and unit with coherent maps
targets.note: Mathlib has monoidal categories with full associator/unitor coherence, which is the abstract shape of the statement, but not for a convolution product on a category of Satake objects that does not exist.

targets.target: Preservation of relative perversity under convolution
targets.note: No perverse t-structure and no convolution in either library.

targets.target: Preservation of coefficient flatness, excluding the Tor obstruction to t-exactness
targets.note: Mathlib has flatness of modules and Tor; the statement here is about flatness of the cohomology sheaves of a convolution of Satake objects, which does not exist.

targets.target: Preservation of ULA under convolution, restricting the operation to Satake objects
targets.note: ULA is absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Aggregate of GS2:correspondences and GS2:Satake-closure
targets.note: Every target of both substages is absent; neither library has Satake objects, convolution of sheaves on v-stacks, relative perversity or ULA.

duplicates.note: GS.1 constructs convolution and the classical equal-characteristic geometric Satake equivalence for the same kind of object over a curve.

targets.target: Factorization of the Grassmannian into products of single-leg Grassmannians over disjoint-leg loci
targets.note: No Beilinson-Drinfeld Grassmannian in either library.

targets.target: Fusion by ULA extension along collision diagonals, its uniqueness and compatibility with repeated collisions
targets.note: ULA is absent; no collision/nearby-cycle formalism for v-stacks exists.

targets.target: The commutativity constraint, with the Koszul/sign and half-Tate normalization making the cohomology fibre functor symmetric monoidal
targets.note: Mathlib has symmetric and braided monoidal categories and symmetric monoidal functors, which is the abstract target shape; the geometric construction of the constraint and the Koszul-sign/half-Tate normalization are absent.

targets.target: coCartesian finite-set functoriality: permutations, maps I -> J, disjoint unions, diagonal pullback, unit insertion and all composition laws
targets.note: No such coherent family exists; Mathlib's Finset/Fintype functoriality is not a family of fusion isomorphisms.

duplicates.note: GS.1 constructs the same collision/factorization maps and asks for the associativity diagrams, not only objectwise isomorphisms, in equal characteristic.

targets.target: Aggregate of GS3:fusion
targets.note: Every target of GS3:fusion is absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Application of the decomposition theorem to finite-type proper models of bounded Witt Schubert spaces over F-bar_q
targets.note: Neither library has the decomposition theorem, perverse sheaves, or Witt Schubert spaces; the whole EDC.7 input is an atlas obligation, not a library fact.

targets.target: Geometric semisimplicity of the rational Satake category via the orbit/IC calculation
targets.note: No intersection complexes in either library (grep -rn -i 'intersection complex' returns nothing).

targets.target: Reductivity of the generic fibre of the Tannakian group
targets.note: There is no Tannakian group of an abstract tensor category in either library, hence nothing whose reductivity could be stated.

duplicates.note: EDC.7 owns pure IC, geometric semisimplicity and the decomposition theorem that this stage applies; it is imported, not restated.

targets.target: Total cohomology fibre functor: exactness, faithfulness, tensor compatibility and duals in the integral category
targets.note: No cohomology of sheaves on v-stacks exists; no fibre functor of any Satake category.

targets.target: Tannakian reconstruction of the affine group scheme from the fibre functor
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves reconstruction for a commutative Hopf algebra H over a field: the points functor of H is isomorphic to the tensor-automorphism functor of scalar extension on finite H-comodules. Mathlib proves Tannaka duality for a finite group. Both start from a group (or Hopf algebra) already given; neither reconstructs an affine group scheme from an abstract rigid tensor category with a fibre functor, which is what this target needs.

targets.target: Identification of the maximal torus and root datum via weight functors, rank-one calculations and simple reflections; identification with the pinned dual group
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a named simply connected root datum for every valid DynkinType and Mathlib has RootPairing.flip, the formal duality that turns a root datum into its dual, so the pinned dual datum as combinatorial data is available. What is absent is any way to produce it from weight functors on a Satake category, and there is no L-group construction: grep -i for LanglandsDual, dualGroup and LGroup in declarations.tsv is empty.

targets.target: Descent for nonsplit G, the geometric Weil action, and the normalization isomorphism involving rho and sqrt(q)
targets.note: There is no Weil group of a local field in either library (grep -i WeilGroup in declarations.tsv is empty).

targets.target: Passage from Z/ell^n to Z_ell and integral recovery from torus/rank-one Levi maps with maximal compact generation (FS VI.9-VI.11)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Naturality for Levi restriction/constant term, products, adjoint isomorphisms and Weil restriction
targets.note: Absent; Tau Ceti has Weil restriction of scalars only in the sense of RepresentationTheory/RelativeNorm, not for dual groups.

targets.target: The Chevalley involution and its compatibility with Verdier duality, inversion of modifications and representation duals
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a Chevalley involution on the Geck-construction carrier of a root system. Verdier duality does not exist in either library (the only 'Verdier' hits are CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsVerdierLeftLocalizing, about localizing subcategories), so the compatibility cannot be stated.

duplicates.note: ES6:functoriality is the declared consumer of the Levi/product/isogeny/Weil-restriction naturality proved here, and restates the same maps on the parameter side.
RG2.5 owns the integral dual group and its pinning, including the remark that square roots used in normalized Satake are coefficient choices; this stage identifies the Tannakian group with it.

targets.target: Frobenius trace of a Satake object on its finite-type special-fibre model
targets.note: No Satake objects and no trace-of-Frobenius function of a complex in either library.

targets.target: The spherical Hecke function algebra of a hyperspecial subgroup and the classical Satake transform
targets.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have the abstract double-coset Hecke ring of a Hecke pair, following Shimura Ch. 3, with the product, associativity, commutativity criterion and degree. That is the right algebra in the commensurable-pair setting, but no Satake transform to the Weyl-invariants of the dual torus is defined, and there is no p-adic reductive group, hyperspecial subgroup or Haar measure normalization to state it with.

targets.target: Convolution/trace and constant-term compatibilities with Haar volume, geometric Frobenius, q^<rho,mu> and the half twist
targets.note: Absent; Mathlib's Haar measure exists for locally compact groups but there is no p-adic reductive group with a hyperspecial subgroup in either library.

duplicates.note: SR.4 owns the classical Satake transform and the isomorphism with the invariant algebra on the dual torus; this stage imports it and only proves the comparison.
GS.5 proves unramified Satake compatibility for the function-field excursion construction, the equal-characteristic analogue of this comparison.

targets.target: Aggregate of GS4:rational-reductivity, GS4:integral-dual-group and GS4:classical-Satake-comparison
targets.note: All three substages are unbuilt; the closest library material is Tau Ceti's Tannakian reconstruction for a known commutative Hopf algebra and its named simply connected root data.

HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. The objects it constructs - Hecke stacks of modifications of G-bundles on the Fargues-Fontaine curve, local shtuka moduli, their J_b(E) and Weil actions, and the Hecke functors T_V built from Satake sheaves - have no counterpart in either library: 'shtuka' and 'Satake' have zero hits in the declaration index and in both Lean trees, and there is no v-stack, diamond or six-operation formalism to state any of them in. The libraries supply only ambient algebra: Mathlib's condensed sets and modules with the free/forgetful adjunction (the coefficient formalism HS1's continuous action needs), its rigid monoidal categories with exact pairings (the abstract shape of HS4's creation/annihilation identities), its adic completion, and its abstract double-coset Hecke ring; Tau Ceti's profinite and pro-p group theory is the group-theoretic side of HS3's pro-p level subgroups. Everything the roadmap actually states is genuinely missing, and its whole upstream chain (RelativeFarguesFontaine, BunGAndNewtonStrata, GeometricSatakeAndFusion, VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories) is missing with it. The nearest existing work in the atlas is the function-field mirror in GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.1-GS.4, which is itself unbuilt.

targets.target: The stack of two G-bundles and an isomorphism away from selected divisors, for a finite leg set I
targets.note: Neither library has G-bundles on the Fargues-Fontaine curve, divisors on it, or any algebraic/v-stack formalism; Mathlib's only 'stack' is CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack, a descent condition on a pseudofunctor.

targets.note: Depends on objects neither library has; dominant cocharacters exist only as root-datum combinatorics in Mathlib's RootPairing and Tau Ceti's root data, with no bounding of modifications.

targets.note: Mathlib's Module.Grassmannian is a functor of submodules with locally free quotient and is not even proved representable (an explicit TODO in the file); it is not the bounded affine Grassmannian.

targets.target: Chains of modifications, composition over disjoint legs and over collisions matching the convolution diagrams
targets.note: Absent; no convolution of sheaves on v-stacks exists in either library.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has forms and Galois descent for representations and algebras (RealForm, GaloisDescent, BrauerGroup), which is the algebraic shadow of inner forms; there is no inner form of a reductive group over a local field and no extension of structure group of a bundle.

duplicates.note: GS.1 constructs bounded global Hecke stacks over powers of a curve with the same source/target/leg structure, in equal characteristic.
GS.2 builds shtuka stacks, modifications and truncations, the function-field counterpart of the correspondence built here.

targets.note: No six-operation formalism on v-stacks in either library; Mathlib's sheaf theory has pushforward and pullback on sites but no exceptional functors.

targets.note: D_lis, ULA and fusion are all absent. Mathlib does have compact objects in a category (CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFilteredColimits / IsCompact-style notions) but not for a category that exists here.

targets.note: Mathlib has condensed sets and condensed R-modules with the free/forgetful adjunction, so the coefficient formalism for a continuous action exists in outline; the Weil group W_E, Drinfeld's lemma and the enriched functor category do not.

LanglandsParameterStacks.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. The central objects - the Weil group of a local field, nonabelian continuous cocycles valued in a dual group, the cocycle scheme Z^1(W_E/P, Ghat) and its quotient stack, the excursion algebra, the coarse invariant quotient, and Perf of the parameter stack - are all absent: there is no Weil group, no L-group or dual group, no quotient stack, no geometric invariant theory, no derived algebraic geometry and no perfect complexes in either library. The libraries do supply real ambient theory that the roadmap will build on: Mathlib's group cohomology and its continuous version for topological groups, extended in Tau Ceti with inflation-restriction, corestriction, Shapiro and long exact sequences, all in abelian coefficients; Mathlib's decomposition and inertia subgroups of a valuation subring (though higher ramification groups are still an explicit TODO, so wild inertia is not there); free groups and presented groups; flatness and the naive cotangent complex; invariant subrings; and Tau Ceti's absolute Galois group with its Krull topology. Two targets the roadmap treats as a matter of specialization are further away than they look: LP3's Weyl and dual-Weyl modules with good filtrations are not Tau Ceti's char-zero Lie-algebra highest-weight theory, nor its GL_n Schur-Weyl `weylModule`, and LP1's local complete intersection structure cannot even be stated, since no complete-intersection predicate exists in Mathlib.

targets.target: The Weil group W_E of a local field with its topology, inertia and wild inertia
targets.note: Mathlib has the decomposition and inertia subgroups of a valuation subring, with the explicit TODO 'Define higher ramification groups in lower numbering', so wild inertia is not there; Tau Ceti has the absolute Galois group with its Krull topology and ramification groups for places of a function field, but nothing for local fields. grep -i for WeilGroup and for 'wild inertia'/'tamely ramified' over both Lean trees returns nothing: there is no Weil group anywhere.

targets.target: Nonabelian continuous/condensed 1-cocycles valued in the L-group, with twisted conjugation
targets.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have a substantial abelian theory: groupCohomology with H0-H2, and continuousCohomology for topological groups acting on topological modules, with Tau Ceti adding inflation, restriction, corestriction, Shapiro, cup products and long exact sequences. All of it is abelian-coefficient. Nonabelian 1-cocycles Z^1(W, Ghat) with twisted conjugation, which is what a parameter is, are absent: grep -i for nonabelian/twistedConjug in declarations.tsv finds nothing relevant.

targets.target: Restriction, scalar extension and sections of the L-group projection; equivalence of the descriptions
targets.note: There is no L-group in either library.

targets.target: The dense discretization W inside W_E/P from tame inertia and Frobenius, and the unique-extension theorem to condensed W_E/P with the topologically unipotent binomial-series argument
targets.note: Absent; there is no tame quotient of a Weil group and no topologically unipotent binomial series in either library.

targets.target: The pinned relation sigma^{-1} tau sigma = tau^q and change-of-tame-generator comparison
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: That layer is the atlas's owner of the local Weil group itself: the carrier localWeilGroup K as the preimage of Z in Zhat, the Weil topology characterized by inertia being an open subgroup with its profinite topology, and local compactness. LP0 states the same carrier as something it uses, so the construction should come from there rather than be rebuilt.
ES1:finite-ramification consumes the same finite-wild-ramification filtration and the uniform wild subgroup for each compact object.
SR.6 also chooses W_F^0 and the normal wild filtration P_F^e and builds cocycle schemes for them, comparing with LP1's Z_ell models.

targets.target: The affine scheme Z^1(W_E/P, Ghat) over Z_ell by finite presentation and equations, its functor of points and independence of W
targets.note: No cocycle scheme for a nonabelian target exists; neither library has a dual group Ghat, so there is nothing to take cocycles in.

targets.target: Gluing the open-and-closed pieces to Z^1(W_E, Ghat)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Flatness and local complete-intersection structure, with dimension dim G on each finite wild piece
targets.note: Mathlib has flatness of modules and algebras and the naive cotangent complex of a presentation, but no local complete intersection predicate at all: grep -i completeIntersection in declarations.tsv returns nothing, so the lci structure cannot even be stated.

targets.target: Twisted conjugation and the quotient stack [Z^1/Ghat], retaining automorphisms
targets.note: There is no quotient stack construction in either library: grep -i quotientStack in declarations.tsv is empty, and Mathlib's IsStack is only a descent condition on a pseudofunctor.

targets.target: Derived affine schemes, fpqc quotient stacks, quasi-coherent modules, perfect complexes and their pullback/descent
targets.note: Derived algebraic geometry is absent: there are no animated/simplicial rings (grep -i for Animation/Anima/SimplicialRing in declarations.tsv is empty) and no perfect complexes (grep -rn -i 'perfect complex' over both Lean trees returns nothing). Mathlib has quasi-coherent sheaves of modules on a scheme but not on a stack.

VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories.summary: Five of the six layers are unbuilt and one, VS2, is partly built. The condensed foundation VS2 asks to consume is genuinely in Mathlib and sorry-free: CondensedMod with its free/forgetful adjunction, Condensed.profiniteFree, Condensed.profiniteSolid as a pointwise right Kan extension, Condensed.profiniteSolidification and the CondensedMod.IsSolid predicate, together with exactness of limits and colimits in condensed modules. The layer's warning is also confirmed by the source: IsSolid's own docstring says it is not the correct definition for a general ring and prescribes the Z[X]-restriction-of-scalars fix, and Mathlib still carries TODOs that no profinite free module is yet proved solid. Everything else is missing. There is no v-topology, perfectoid space, diamond or Artin v-stack in either library, no six operations and no exceptional functors, no universal local acyclicity, no hyperbolic localization, no Drinfeld lemma, no solid tensor product or internal Hom, no D_solid or D_lis, no smooth representations of locally pro-p groups, and no Bernstein-Zelevinsky or Verdier duality. What the libraries contribute beyond VS2 is ambient machinery the roadmap will build on rather than targets: Mathlib's sheaves on sites and its IsStack descent condition, pretriangulated categories and t-structures, group cohomology as derived invariants, formal smoothness, and Z_ell; Tau Ceti's pro-p group theory is the group-theoretic side of VS4's level subgroups.

targets.target: Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas condition (FS IV.1); atlas independence and stability under fibre products
targets.note: Mathlib's IsStack is the descent condition on a pseudofunctor over a site; it is not an algebraic or v-stack, has no diagonal or atlas notion, and there is no v-topology, no perfectoid space and no diamond in either library.

targets.target: Smooth-lisse descent of the enhanced coefficient category and extension of the allowed operations
targets.note: Absent; there is no enhanced (stable infinity-categorical) coefficient category in either library.

targets.target: Pullback, exceptional pullback and their normalization for smooth atlases; comparison with small-v-stack ECD categories
targets.note: Neither library has exceptional functors f^! or f_!; Mathlib's sheaf operations on a site are pushforward/pullback only.

targets.target: Partial compact-support functors pi-sharp of FS IV.5 for stacks outside the representable ECD class, with independence of presentation, adjunctions and base change
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: S2 handles compactifiable maps and small v-stacks, and S4 cohomological smoothness; VS0 extends that representable ECD class to Artin v-stacks rather than rebuilding it.
BG2:smooth-Artin proves Bun_G is an Artin v-stack using this definition, so the definition has one declared owner and one immediate applier.

targets.target: Relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with overconvergence, geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions (FS IV.2)
targets.note: grep -rn -i 'universally locally acyclic' over both Lean trees returns nothing, and neither library has the etale cohomology of adic spaces in which it would be stated.

targets.target: Base change, composition, descent, tensor and relative-dual properties of ULA with their compactness hypotheses
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3-IV.4 for relative section functors on Fargues-Fontaine curves; the tangent/cohomology calculation, positive-slope condition and resulting cohomological smoothness
targets.note: Mathlib has formal smoothness of algebras by the infinitesimal lifting criterion, and a Jacobian criterion for smooth ring maps, but the Jacobian criterion here is FS IV.4 for the Banach-Colmez section functor of a bundle on the Fargues-Fontaine curve, and that curve does not exist in either library.

targets.target: Attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison map of FS IV.6 with equivariance and boundedness
targets.note: Absent from both trees.

targets.target: Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from a fundamental-group product claim
targets.note: Absent; there is no partial Frobenius and no Weil group in either library.

duplicates.note: GS.4 proves Drinfeld's lemma in the lisse/finite-rank setting for the function-field Hecke-finite application, the same theorem in the equal-characteristic mirror.

targets.target: Mathlib's CondensedMod with its free/forgetful adjunction and its profinite free-module and solidification maps
targets.note: Present and sorry-free exactly as the layer describes. Condensed sets are sheaves on CompHaus for the coherent topology, CondensedMod R their module objects; free/forget is an adjunction, profiniteSolid is the pointwise right Kan extension of the free functor on finite sets along FintypeCat.toProfinite, and profiniteSolidification is the natural map R[S] -> R[S]^solid.

targets.target: Correcting CondensedMod.IsSolid: first the finite-type Z-algebra construction, then general coefficient rings by restriction of scalars
targets.note: CondensedMod.IsSolid exists but its own docstring says 'This is not the correct definition of solid R-modules for a general R' and prescribes precisely the Z[X]-restriction-of-scalars fix the layer asks for. So the predicate is there and the correction is not. Mathlib also records two open TODOs next to it: that ((profiniteSolid Z).obj S).IsSolid and the F_p analogue are unproved, so not a single profinite free module is yet known to be solid.

targets.target: The solidification universal property and derived solid tensor/Hom, with generators and exactness for FS VII.1
targets.note: Mathlib has AB-style exactness of limits and colimits in condensed modules and a monoidal structure on light condensed modules, but no solid tensor product, no internal Hom of solid modules and no universal property of solidification.

targets.target: Finite/cofiltered limit and completion comparisons with actual topological modules
targets.note: Absent; Mathlib relates condensed sets to topological spaces (TopComparison, TopCatAdjunction) but has no comparison of solid modules with topological modules.

targets.target: D_solid(X,Lambda) on a small v-stack over the appropriate cutoffs, four operations and relative homology f-sharp (FS VII.2-VII.3)
targets.note: Absent; there are no v-stacks in either library.

targets.target: Solid projection/base-change identities, comparison with torsion D_et, and the dualizability theorem of VII.4-VII.5
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: HR.2 names the solid-tensor comparison of this stage as an input it extends in a bounded-below setting, so the solid tensor product has a declared consumer outside this roadmap.

targets.target: The discrete Z_ell-algebra Lambda read as the condensed extension Z_ell tensor Lambda_disc
targets.note: Mathlib has Z_ell as PadicInt with its topology, and condensed modules over a ring, so both factors exist; the condensed tensor product of the two, with the discretization functor, is not constructed.

targets.target: D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated, representable, ell-cohomologically smooth f
targets.note: Absent; there are no Artin v-stacks, no f-sharp, and no stable infinity-categories in either library.

targets.target: The right adjoint of the inclusion, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/pushforward
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Comparison of ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through the fully faithful functors of VII.6
targets.note: Absent; none of the four categories exists.

targets.target: Reduction and scalar extension in their established range; the solid/lisse localization for rational coefficients
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: L0 defines D_et(X,Lambda) for an I-adically complete coefficient ring, the adic coefficient category this stage compares with; VS3 imports it rather than rebuilding it.
C7 owns constructible and perfect-constructible coefficients on diamonds with their v-descent, which is the small-v-stack layer of the coefficient comparison VS3 extends to Artin v-stacks.

targets.target: Identification of D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations, for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda
targets.note: Tau Ceti has pro-p groups with their Sylow, Frattini and maximal-pro-p theory and Mathlib has the category Rep k G of linear representations with its derived functors, but smooth representations of a locally pro-p group are not defined in either library (grep -i smoothRepresentation/SmoothRep in declarations.tsv is empty) and D_et([*/H]) does not exist.

targets.target: Both functors by continuous torsor descent; pullback as forgetting the action and invariants as the derived pushforward
targets.note: Mathlib's group cohomology is the derived functor of invariants for an abstract group, which is the algebraic half of the statement; the geometric half, descent along a continuous H-torsor of v-sheaves, is absent.

targets.target: Application to J_b(E) and the connected-kernel invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b; extension to D_lis in the range of VII.7
targets.note: Absent; there is no Bun_G, no Newton stratification and no J_b in either library.

targets.target: Localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the HN strata using justified exhaustions
targets.note: Mathlib has pretriangulated categories with distinguished triangles, which is the ambient formalism, but no semiorthogonal decompositions and no Harder-Narasimhan stratification of a stack of bundles.

targets.target: Characterization of compact objects by compact restrictions with finite stratum support and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p open subgroups
targets.note: Absent; compact induction of smooth representations does not exist in either library.

duplicates.note: SR.0-SR.2 own the smooth-representation category and the compact-induction generators that this identification is stated against; the layer says explicitly these are the same objects.

C9 proves compact generation and the characterization of compact objects for D_et on diamonds under uniform cohomological-dimension bounds; VS4 restates the same characterization for the Bun_G strata.

targets.target: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects via the partial-support functor, with biduality and the basic-stratum comparison
targets.note: Absent; grep -rn -i 'Bernstein' over both Lean trees returns nothing, and there is no Bun_G.

targets.target: Verdier duality on ULA objects
targets.note: The only occurrences of 'Verdier' in either library are the left/right Verdier localizing subcategory classes, which are about Verdier quotients of triangulated categories, not about the dualizing-complex duality D = RHom(-, omega); ULA objects are absent too.

targets.target: Equivalence of ULA with perfection of K-invariants on every stratum for every pro-p open K
targets.note: Absent; neither ULA, nor perfect complexes, nor K-invariants of smooth representations exist in either library.

targets.target: Scalar-extension and Hecke-use compatibility; admissibility as perfect invariants
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: ES6:duality is the declared consumer of the Bernstein-Zelevinsky and Verdier duality statements built here.

EDC.1 constructs f^!, the dualizing object, D_X = RHom(-, K_X) and biduality on the scheme side; VS5's Verdier duality on ULA objects is the v-stack instance of the same duality, so the dualizing formalism has an upstream owner.

SR.5 constructs Bernstein-Zelevinsky derivatives and top derivatives for GL_n over the integral coefficient rings; it overlaps the representation-theoretic half of the Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality built here.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CFSGStatement.summary: This roadmap is substantially built in Tau Ceti, and the whole CFSG directory is sorry-free. I0 is complete: PrimePower, LieTypeIndex with its validity and duplicate predicates, ValidLieTypeIndex, SuzukiReeIndex, GraphTwistedIndex, SporadicName with card_sporadicName = 26 proved by decide, CFSGIndex, the numbered data with rank defined as dynkinType.rank, the algebraic-closure Closure, and all six pinned permutations with their Cartan-matrix invariance. S0 and S1 are complete too: the Relator expression type with its compilation theorem, the GroupPresentation metadata record with the layer's exact fields and no checksum, and all twenty-six transcribed sporadic presentations with their count checks, including the Monster by the Y443 route with Ivanov's central relator appended, exactly as S1 prescribes. The Lie-type lane is built for thirteen of the seventeen constructors. Carriers, Steinberg maps, fixed points and candidate groups exist for A, 2A, B, C, D, 2D, E6, 2E6, E7, E8, F4, G2 and the Suzuki family, on the spin, symplectic, minuscule, Geck and standard-linear carriers the L0 table designates, with the root-datum Steinberg map complete for every valid index. What is genuinely missing: the tripled D4 carrier and hence the 3D4 branch; the short-root G2 and F4 carriers as group schemes with their special isogenies, and hence the Ree and Tits branches (their short-root modules exist only as Lie-algebra representations); the uniform ValidLieTypeIndex.Group; L5 in its entirety, and with it the pinned Chevalley--Demazure group scheme over Z that L0's pinned route and L1's uniqueness theorem cite from the reductive-groups roadmap; and A0's CFSGIndex.Group and ClassificationStatement. One A0 target the document treats as work is already done and more generally than stated: TauCeti.exists_mulEquiv_of_forall_finite_isSimpleGroup_zero is classificationStatement_of_zero for an arbitrary indexed family.

targets.target: PrimePower, LieTypeIndex, InStandardRange, IsDuplicateRepresentative, Valid, ValidLieTypeIndex
targets.note: All present with parameters carried as data on a seventeen-constructor inductive, exactly as the layer asks, and each predicate is decidable (DecidablePred instances beside each). LieTypeIndex.Valid at Index.lean:190 is InStandardRange and not IsDuplicateRepresentative.

targets.target: UsesHalfFrobenius, SuzukiReeIndex, GraphTwistedIndex as the validated subtypes
targets.note: SuzukiReeIndex and GraphTwistedIndex are the two subtypes of ValidLieTypeIndex cut out by UsesHalfFrobenius and its negation, so the layer's rule that only these may be passed to a half-Frobenius or a diagram permutation is enforced by the types. The layer's warning is also respected: the file proves not_usesHalfFrobenius_of_isTypeE6 and the like, so the predicate is false on the exceptional types.

targets.target: SporadicName with cardinality 26, and CFSGIndex
targets.note: card_sporadicName : Fintype.card SporadicName = 26 is proved by decide. CFSGIndex has the four constructors cyclic/alternating/lie/sporadic with the prime and degree-at-least-five proof fields, and no Finite or IsSimpleGroup instance attached.

targets.target: The numbered data read off an index: dynkinType, dynkinType_valid, rank defined as dynkinType.rank, characteristic, characteristic_prime, fieldOrder
targets.note: rank is literally `abbrev rank (d : ValidLieTypeIndex) : Nat := d.dynkinType.rank`, so it is not tabulated a second time, as the layer requires. dynkinType lands in the root-systems roadmap's DynkinType.

targets.target: Closure = AlgebraicClosure (ZMod characteristic) with its Field, IsAlgClosed and CharP instances from Mathlib
targets.note: Closure.lean defines the abbreviation and then checks by `example ... := inferInstance` that Field, IsAlgClosed and CharP are all inherited, which is exactly the glue the layer asks for.

targets.target: The pinned permutations graphPermA, graphPermD, graphPermE6, trialityPermD4, lengthPermRankTwo, lengthPermF4
targets.note: All six are in TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/DiagramPermutations.lean (lengthPermRankTwo at line 78), each with its order lemma (graphPermA_sq, trialityPermD4_pow_three, ...) and its Cartan-matrix invariance (cartanMatrix_A_graphPermA at 227, cartanMatrix_D4_trialityPermD4 at 284).

targets.target: No second table of long simple roots: the convention stated against DynkinType.IsLongSimpleRoot
targets.note: The length-exchanging property of the two length permutations is proved against the upstream predicate rather than tabulated, as the layer requires.

targets.target: Executable examples for the small-field exclusions and the duplicate table
targets.note: Index.lean carries worked `example`s at lines 1410-1450 discharged by decide, covering A_1(2) and A_1(4) excluded, twistedA 2 q3 valid, B_2(2) excluded, B_2(3) invalid as a duplicate and C_3(2) excluded.

targets.target: Type A carrier SL_{n+1} = TauCeti.SlStd with its root subgroups, and the pinned graph automorphism for twistedA
targets.note: Built and sorry-free: the standard carrier, its all-root subgroup family, the signed-antidiagonal graph automorphism on points, and the index-level AmbientGroup/simpleRootSubgroup the layer names.

targets.target: Type B full-weight spin carrier at every rank, type C symplectic carrier, type D spin carrier with its fork-exchange graph automorphism
targets.note: All four rows of the carrier table are built, each with AmbientGroup, simpleRootSubgroup and a Frobenius on points, and with finiteness of the Frobenius fixed subgroup proved (finite_fixedSubgroup_frobenius in each SpinCarrier/FixedPoints.lean).

targets.target: E6 27-dimensional minuscule carrier, doubled minuscule carrier for twistedE6, E7 56-dimensional minuscule carrier
targets.note: All three exist with their numbered simple root subgroups; the doubled E6 carrier carries its graph automorphism as a signed permutation of the weight basis (E6DoubledMinuscule.GraphAutomorphism.lean), which is the mechanism the layer prescribes.

targets.target: Geck carrier for E8, F4 and G2, with the full-weight span statement that selects exactly those three types
targets.note: Built exactly as designed, including DynkinType.span_range_geckWeight_eq_top_iff, which is the proof that the adjoint module is full-weight precisely in E8, F4 and G2 and hence that the Geck carrier is the simply connected form only there.

targets.target: The rank-two type-C carrier for the Suzuki branch, with the B2/C2 node adapter
targets.note: carrierNode is exactly the named adapter the layer prescribes, B2 0 |-> C2 1 and B2 1 |-> C2 0, with carrierNode_apply and the proof that it preserves the long/short designation.

targets.target: The tripled D4 carrier (toral closure of 8v + 8s + 8c in GL_24) with triality as a numbered symmetry
targets.note: The diagram permutation exists and its Cartan-matrix invariance is proved, but no tripled D4 carrier exists: grep -i triality over declarations.tsv finds only the index predicate IsTypeTrialityD4, the diagram permutation, and GraphTwistedIndex.diagramPerm_trialityD4. There is no group-level triality and no TypeTrialityD4LieIndex.AmbientGroup.

targets.target: Short-root G2 carrier over F_3 and short-root F4 carrier over F_2 as closed subgroup schemes of GL_7 and GL_26
targets.note: Both short-root modules are built at the Lie-algebra level: explicit integral Chevalley matrices on the 7- and 26-element weight diagrams, the Serre relations, the divided squares and the induced representation. What is missing is the group-scheme step, the closed subgroup scheme over the prime field generated by the reduced root subgroups and torus, its ordered weight basis and the identification C used to define the special isogeny.

targets.target: The pinned route: the simply connected Chevalley--Demazure group scheme over Z for every untwisted Dynkin type, its base change and points, and root-subgroup maps x_alpha
targets.note: The root-systems input the pinned route consumes is built: a named simply connected root datum for every valid DynkinType, with its Bourbaki-numbered base. The reductive-groups Layer 9 output is not: there is no pinned Chevalley--Demazure group scheme over Z in the library. grep -i for chevalleyGroupScheme/ChevalleyDemazure/pinnedGroupScheme in declarations.tsv returns nothing, and the Kostant toral-closure machinery (TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/UniversalEnveloping/Kostant/RootSubgroup/Scheme/ToralClosure) is what the explicit carriers are built from instead.

duplicates.note: Layer 9 of the reductive-groups roadmap owns the pinned Chevalley--Demazure group schemes, base change, points and root subgroups that the pinned route here consumes; this layer explicitly says it consumes rather than duplicates them.
Layer 6 of the root-systems roadmap owns DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum and the Bourbaki numbering this layer's Fin indices carry.

targets.target: Frob_q on points, and the Steinberg map as gamma o Frob_q for the graph-twisted families
targets.note: The root-datum layer is complete for every valid index, and the group-level Frobenius and graph automorphism exist for type A/twistedA, B, C, D/twistedD, E6/twistedE6, E7 and the unimodular exceptionals. Composition order is handled exactly as the table requires: TypeALieIndex.steinberg_eq_graphAut_comp_frobenius at TypeA.lean:319 with the commutation graphAut_comp_frobenius at 310.

targets.target: gamma^2 = 1 for 2A, 2D, 2E6 and gamma^3 = 1 for 3D4, with gamma commuting with Frob_q
targets.note: The order and commutation relations are proved at group level for the involutive families (2A, 2D, 2E6) and at root-datum level for all of them via the twist order. The 3D4 case has no group-level gamma, because its carrier does not exist (see L0).

targets.target: The diagram permutations pinned as Fin data, each proved an automorphism of the Cartan matrix
targets.note: diagramPerm is total on GraphTwistedIndex, so the table is exhaustive exactly as the layer requires, and the Suzuki--Ree branches cannot reach it. Every permutation carries its Cartan-matrix invariance, which is the 'proved to be an automorphism of the Cartan matrix' obligation.

targets.target: The defining equations gamma(x_alpha(t)) = x_{gamma alpha}(t) on simple roots and Frob_q(x_alpha(t)) = x_alpha(t^q) on every root
targets.note: Proved on the numbered simple root subgroups for every family whose carrier exists, and restricted to simple roots exactly as the layer demands. Missing for the 3D4 branch, and the general-root form with the sign epsilon_alpha is recorded only for SlStd's all-root family, not uniformly.

targets.target: Uniqueness of gamma from its action on the pinned simple root subgroups (the isomorphism theorem for pinned groups)
targets.note: This is cited as a Layer 9 target upstream, and it is not in the library: there is no pinned Chevalley--Demazure group scheme and no isomorphism theorem for pinned groups.

duplicates.note: The isomorphism theorem for pinned groups, which gives uniqueness of gamma, is a Layer 9 target cited here rather than reproved.

targets.target: Selecting tau_X for a given SuzukiReeIndex and taking the odd power steinberg(m) = tau_X^{2m+1}
targets.note: The selection and odd power are complete at root-datum level for all four branches (suzuki, reeG2, reeF4, tits), with SuzukiReeIndex.halfExponent and fieldExponent_eq_two_mul_halfExponent_add_one pinning 2m+1. At group level only the Suzuki branch exists, because only the rank-two symplectic carrier has a special isogeny; reeG2, reeF4 and tits have no group-level steinberg.

targets.target: The square relation steinberg(m)^2 = Frob_{p^{2m+1}}, inherited from tau_X^2 = Frob_p
targets.note: Proved at root-datum level for all four branches and at group level for the Suzuki branch. The other three branches wait on their carriers.

targets.target: The identifying action tau_X(x_alpha(t)) = x_{alpha-bar}(t) on long and x_{alpha-bar}(t^p) on short simple roots, with the length map proved to exchange lengths
targets.note: lengthPerm is total on SuzukiReeIndex with lengthPerm_suzuki/reeG2/reeF4/tits, isLongSimpleRoot_lengthPerm is the required exchange proof stated against the upstream predicate, and the exponent convention (1 on long, p on short) is SuzukiReeIndex.rootLength with exponent_mul_exponent_lengthPerm proving the two exponents multiply to p. The group-level equations exist only for the Suzuki branch.

targets.target: The special isogeny tau_X of the ambient group, for B2 in characteristic two, G2 in characteristic three and F4 in characteristic two
targets.note: Only the B2 (Sp_4, characteristic two) case exists, with the 2x2-minor construction and its root-subgroup equations. The G2 and F4 special isogenies are not in the library; their short-root modules exist as Lie-algebra representations but not as group schemes carrying an isogeny. This is a Layer 9 obligation upstream, which this layer says it consumes.

targets.target: The B2/C2 adapter and the m >= 1 restriction that excludes the solvable Sz(2)
targets.note: carrierNode is public in TypeB/Two.lean with carrierNode_apply, and its compatibility with the length permutation is used inside Suzuki/Basic.lean to derive the public steinberg_simpleRootSubgroup, which states the branch's equations in the B2 numbering after the adapter, exactly as the layer requires. The small-field exclusion is carried by InStandardRange, whose suzuki branch requires 1 <= m; UnimodularLieIndex.reeG2 and reeF4 likewise take an explicit 1 <= m. Mathlib's separate suzukiGroup construction (PR 42043) is not in the pinned baseline, so nothing here needs to avoid it.

duplicates.note: Layer 9 owns the special isogeny tau_X of pinned group schemes, its action on long and short root subgroups and tau_X^2 = Frob_p; this layer selects it and takes the odd power.

targets.target: The fixed subgroup of an endomorphism as F.eqLocus (MonoidHom.id G)
targets.note: Defined exactly as the layer prescribes, with the API the Suzuki--Ree branches need (fixedSubgroup_le_fixedSubgroup_pow, which places the fixed group of an odd half-Frobenius power inside that of the corresponding Frobenius).

targets.target: The candidate group [H,H] / Z([H,H]), with the centre taken of the derived subgroup
targets.note: FixedPointCandidate F is the derived subgroup of fixedSubgroup F modulo the centre of that derived subgroup, in the order the layer specifies, with a congr transport along an isomorphism of the two data.

targets.target: A per-family Group with its Group instance, for every branch of ValidLieTypeIndex.steinberg
targets.note: Ten per-family Group definitions exist: TypeA (covering A and 2A), TypeB, TypeC, TypeD, TypeTwistedD, TypeE6, TypeTwistedE6, TypeE7, UnimodularExceptional (E8, F4, G2) and Suzuki. Four of the seventeen constructors have none: trialityD4, reeG2, reeF4 and tits, all blocked on their L0/L2 carriers. Worth recording against the layer's closing remark: the (B,N)-pair theory it dismisses as an external Mathlib PR is already in Tau Ceti as TauCeti.TitsSystem with a Bruhat directory, so the related structure theory is present even though, as the layer says, this lane does not depend on it.

targets.target: The uniform ValidLieTypeIndex.Group assembled by cases from the per-family definitions
targets.note: Absent: grep for TauCeti.ValidLieTypeIndex.(Group|steinberg|AmbientGroup|FixedPoints) in declarations.tsv returns nothing, so the uniform assembly has not been made. It cannot be, until the four missing branches have carriers.

targets.target: A MulEquiv e from each explicit AmbientGroup to the points of the pinned Chevalley--Demazure group with e(x i t) = x' i t and e(F g) = F'(e g)
targets.note: No such identification exists for any family. The pinned side does not exist either: there is no pinned Chevalley--Demazure group scheme over Z in the library, so, as the layer itself notes, the signature cannot yet be stated.

targets.target: The pinned side's F' built independently by the L1 or L2 recipe on the pinned carrier
targets.note: Absent, for the same reason.

targets.target: Transport of FixedPoints and Group along e by the fixed-point recipe's transport lemmas
targets.note: The transport machinery is already built: FixedPointCandidate.congr carries the candidate group along an isomorphism intertwining the two endomorphisms, with congr_refl, congr_trans and congr_symm. Only the equivalence e it would be applied to is missing.

duplicates.note: This milestone depends entirely on Layer 9 of the reductive-groups roadmap supplying the pinned points; it is separately claimable for exactly that reason.

targets.target: The stored Relator expression type with generator, inverse, product, power and commutator constructors
targets.note: All five constructors are present, with the commutator fixed to Mathlib's convention and a docstring telling a transcriber how to convert a source using the opposite one.

targets.target: The semantic form PresentationWord, the compilation Relator.toWord, and the associated PresentedGroup
targets.note: PresentationWord is List (alpha x Bool) with FreeGroup.mk's sign convention, toWord compiles each constructor, and GroupPresentation.Group is PresentedGroup of the relator set built from the compiled words, exactly the definition the layer displays.

targets.target: Relator.toWord_toFreeGroup: the compiled word denotes what the expression denotes
targets.note: Both the per-relator statement and its packaged form for a whole presentation are proved, so the step between what a reviewer checks and what is defined is justified, which is what the layer asks for.

targets.target: Metadata: generator names, bibliographic source and locator, generator convention, transcription notes, expected generator and relator counts, with decidable count checks and no checksum
targets.note: Every field the layer lists is a field of the structure, the arity is the length of generatorNames and is not recorded twice, there is deliberately no checksum field (the docstring says so and gives the layer's reason), and matchesMetadata is the decidable two-count check. The file adds relatorLetters and totalLength as a third decidable check against a published presentation length.

targets.target: A 26-row source manifest: name, exact source, locator, generator names and expected counts for each sporadic group, with semi-presentations rejected
targets.note: The manifest is realized as the metadata of the twenty-six presentations themselves: each of the group-specific modules carries source, sourceLocator, generatorNames, generatorConvention, transcriptionNotes and the two expected counts, and presentation_matchesMetadata checks the counts for all 26 names at once. The GroupPresentation docstring states the rule that a source must be a full presentation and not a semi-presentation. Only the manifest's review-status column is bookkeeping rather than mathematics, and that part is process by the layer's own description.

targets.target: Every SporadicName.presentation branch filled with the complete signed relator words
targets.note: A total function on all 26 names, each branch dispatching to an independently transcribed GroupPresentation in its own module (26 files under CFSG/Sporadic/), with no sorry anywhere in the directory.

targets.target: The Monster by the Y443 presentation: 12 generators, Coxeter relations, spider relation and Z = 1, giving 80 relators
targets.note: Exactly the construction the layer prescribes and neither substitute it forbids: the twelve-node Y443 diagram, 12 + 11 + 55 = 78 Coxeter relators, the spider word (a b1 c1 a b2 c2 a b3 c3)^10 giving Bray's 79-relator M x 2, and Ivanov's central f312 = (a b3 c3 d3 b1 c1 b2)^9 appended as the 80th to pass to M. The module docstring carries Ivanov's page references for the definition, the centrality lemma and the SS3.9 identification.

targets.target: The Baby Monster by its Y433 presentation and every other branch to the same standard
targets.note: Present, along with the Fischer groups from smaller Y-diagrams with the spider relation and the remaining 23 names; every module records a cited source rather than an ATLAS semi-presentation.

targets.target: The recorded relator count checked against the transcribed list, for every name
targets.note: presentation_matchesMetadata is proved by cases on all 26 names, each discharged by that group's own matchesMetadata lemma, so the generator and relator counts are checked uniformly.

targets.target: No order, finiteness, simplicity or isomorphism assertion for the presented groups
targets.note: Respected: SporadicName.Group is just presentation.Group, and the module docstrings state explicitly that no order, finiteness or simplicity result is asserted. The independent source-to-Lean read-through and the permutation-group cross-check the layer asks for are review artifacts, not Lean targets, and are outside the library by design.

targets.target: CFSGIndex.Group by cases with its dependent Group instance
targets.note: The index type and three of the four branches' carriers exist (ZMod p, Mathlib's alternatingGroup, and SporadicName.Group), but CFSGIndex.Group itself is not defined anywhere: grep -rn CFSGIndex over the Tau Ceti tree finds only Index.lean's definition and two docstring references saying the assembly is still to come. The Lie branch could not be assembled anyway, since ValidLieTypeIndex.Group does not exist (see L3).

targets.target: The named ClassificationStatement as an existential over CFSGIndex
targets.note: Absent: grep -rn -i classificationStatement over the Tau Ceti tree finds only a docstring in SimpleGroupUniverse.lean saying the theorem will be the specialization of the general one once CFSGIndex.Group is assembled.

targets.target: classificationStatement_of_zero: ClassificationStatement.{0} implies ClassificationStatement.{u}
targets.note: The mathematical content of this target is already proved, and in more generality than the roadmap states it: for any family C : iota -> Type v of groups, if every finite simple group in Type is isomorphic to some C i then so is every finite simple group in any universe. The proof is the Shrink.{0} argument the layer describes, transporting simplicity along Shrink.mulEquiv. Specializing it to CFSGIndex.Group is all that remains, and that waits on the previous two targets.
